definition: Scientific explanation is a foundational concept in science learning that involves understanding and explaining phenomena in scientifically meaningful ways. In education, how well students master it is treated as an important sign of their understanding of the nature of science.

reasons: The packet supports that “scientific explanation” is a core concept in science education and that mastery is crucial for understanding the nature of science, but it does not explicitly support the definition’s claim that scientific explanation “involves understanding and explaining phenomena in scientifically meaningful ways.”
Because the packet does not define “scientifically meaningful ways” or characterize scientific explanation in those terms, that substantive part of the definition is unsupported.

The definition adds an unsupported gloss by saying scientific explanation involves ‘understanding and explaining phenomena in scientifically meaningful ways’; the packet only says it is a core concept in science education, without defining it that way.
The wording ‘foundational concept in science learning’ is broader than the packet’s claim and is not directly supported as stated.

The sentence about students’ mastery being an important sign of their understanding of the nature of science is only partly supported; the packet says mastery is crucial for a deep understanding of the nature of science, not that it is specifically used as a sign or indicator.
